oewn-02605633-v.learner: to do something, or put it into action.
examples: They took steps to repair the damage.
She took action as soon as she was asked.

oewn-02003830-v.learner: to bring a person to a place, going there with them.
examples: Mr. Bennet was glad to take his guest into the drawing-room again
He took the children to the river.

oewn-02113499-v.learner: to feel something, live through it, or put up with it.
examples: she took an epicurean delight in dissecting, in displaying, in setting at work her fools and her mean persons
He took the pain without complaint.

oewn-02214718-v.learner: to use something, or accept it, because it serves some purpose.
examples: he took the opportunity of paying the parting civilities
She took the risk and went anyway.

oewn-01986409-v.learner: to move into a place or position and fill it.
examples: she again took her seat at the head of her table
they would have taken up their abode with her

oewn-10306910-n.learner: a grown person who is male, not a woman.
examples: What an agreeable man Sir William is
Is not he a charming man?

oewn-10308700-n.learner: this word used to mean any human being at all, male or female.
examples: Man has always feared the dark.
No man can live without hope.

connotation.why: names all people with the word for males

oewn-10308837-n.learner: a male worker or helper who is under someone else's orders.
examples: The captain sent two of his men ahead.
He waited all week for word from his man in the north.

oewn-00059624-r.learner: by a large amount; a lot.
examples: Upon the whole, I am much pleased with him.
You have employed your time much better.

oewn-00023283-r.learner: used before a noun to say that something is so in every way that counts, though not completely.
examples: when I am in town, it is pretty much the same
The town looked much the same as before.
She does not go out much these days.
They did not speak much during the journey.

oewn-01773236-s.learner: belonging to that person, or done for that person, and used after a word like my, her, or their.
examples: Mr. Bingley did not do justice to his own disposition
she may like to have her own way

oewn-01558903-a.learner: used with things you cannot count, to say there is only a small amount, or almost none, or, with "a" in front, at least some.
examples: Mr. Bennet indeed said little
there cannot be too little said on the subject

oewn-01394303-a.learner: smaller or fewer in size, number, or amount than is usual.
examples: They rented a little house near the sea.
She packed her things into a little bag.

oewn-01653473-s.learner: young and not yet grown, said of children and animals.
examples: Her little brother starts school this year.
A little dog followed us home.
He replied, and was again silent.
The families who had been in town for the winter came back again

oewn-15180180-n.learner: the time the Earth takes to turn around once, which is twenty-four hours.
examples: not a day went by without a solitary walk
which was dated a day later

oewn-15148032-n.learner: a moment or a stretch of time.
examples: There will come a day when you understand this.
He hoped that one day they would meet again.

oewn-15274047-n.learner: the stretch of time when someone or something was alive or had power.
examples: the false realism of our own day
He was a famous singer in his day.

oewn-00600349-v.learner: to come to know something, usually by chance.
examples: I have heard, indeed, that she is uncommonly improved within this year or two.
she had heard that Miss Darcy was exceedingly proud

oewn-02174146-v.learner: to take in a sound with your ears.
examples: She could hear the rain on the roof.
I heard a door close downstairs.

oewn-02175483-v.learner: to listen to something and give it your attention.
examples: let us hear all the particulars
Sit down and hear what she has to say.

oewn-00112352-r.learner: put before a word to say that something is greater than all the others.
examples: It seems to me the most perfect, the most characteristic, the most eminently quintessential of its author's works
She is the most careful driver I know.

oewn-00032295-r.learner: put before a word to make it stronger, meaning very.
examples: It must have been a most agreeable surprise to Mr. Bingley
It certainly is a most iniquitous affair

oewn-00073433-r.learner: used of things done or happening, to say almost, but not quite, all of it.
examples: Most everyone had already left.
Most all of the seats were taken.

oewn-01651383-a.learner: in the early part of life or growth, said of living things and above all of people.
examples: And there are several of the young men, too, that she likes very much.
I should be sorry, you know, to think ill of a young man who has lived so long in Derbyshire.

oewn-01654162-s.learner: seeming young, and full of strength and freshness.
examples: At seventy he was still young in spirit.
She has a young face and a quick step.

connotation.why: praises someone as fresh and full of life

examples: The night was still young when they left.
It is a young company, only two years old.
